documents.title: Obstetrics Prenatal Update
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL UPDATE TO PRIMARY CARE
Date of visit: 2023-02-24

G1 at 20 weeks by early ultrasound dating, conceived with ovulation induction. Doing well.

Anatomy ultrasound today: single live intrauterine fetus, growth appropriate for gestational age, anatomy survey complete and normal. Placenta posterior and well clear of the cervix. Amniotic fluid normal.

History reviewed: type 1 von Willebrand disease (hematology aware of the pregnancy), Kallmann syndrome, iron deficiency on oral iron. Latex allergy flagged on her chart and on the labor unit.

Plan: routine prenatal visits; no further ultrasound planned unless there is a clinical question. Delivery at our hospital's labor unit with hematology available.

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 2023-07-01  Discharged: 2023-07-03

Patient: 32-year-old G1, term, conceived with ovulation induction. Type 1 von Willebrand disease, Kallmann syndrome, chronic iron deficiency on oral iron. Latex allergy (contact dermatitis); no drug allergies.

COURSE
Presented in spontaneous labor. Labor progressed on its own with no induction, augmentation or instruments. At 03:40 she had a vaginal delivery of a healthy boy. Oxytocin was given for the third stage only. The placenta delivered a few minutes later; on inspection its margin was irregular and a vessel coursed out onto the membranes.

Within about half an hour she was bleeding heavily. Pressure fell to 80/50 with a heart rate of 120; she became agitated and confused, and her skin was cool and clammy. The fundus could not be felt abdominally and a large, red, rounded mass was protruding from the vagina - acute uterine inversion. Hemoglobin had been 12 on admission and was 9 at that point; platelets 250, INR 1.1. Type A positive.

She was taken to the operating room and the uterus was manually replaced under anesthesia. Her pressure reached a low of 80/40 during the reduction, and she received 4 units of packed red cells. After replacement the uterus was firm and of expected postpartum size, with no vaginal or cervical lacerations, but bleeding persisted despite oxytocin and did not respond to fundal massage. Afebrile, BP 92/60, HR 122; hemoglobin 7.4. Given her von Willebrand disease, intravenous desmopressin was given on hematology's advice and the bleeding settled over the next hour.

She recovered on the postpartum unit, ambulating and tolerating diet. Breastfeeding was started with lactation support.

DIAGNOSES: vaginal delivery at term; acute uterine inversion, manually reduced; acute postpartum hemorrhage with hypovolemic shock; acute blood-loss anemia, transfused; type 1 von Willebrand disease.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; vitamin D3 2000 IU daily; desmopressin nasal spray as needed for bleeding.

FOLLOW-UP: obstetrics postpartum visit; primary care in 1-2 weeks for anemia. Return for heavy bleeding, fever or dizziness.

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal views. Postpartum uterus, enlarged as expected for day 3 after vaginal delivery, normal in orientation. Endometrial cavity contains a small amount of fluid; no echogenic mass and no internal vascularity to suggest retained placental tissue. Ovaries unremarkable. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: No sonographic evidence of retained products of conception.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Date of service: 2023-07-04

CC: postpartum bleeding.

HPI: 32F, day 3 after a vaginal delivery complicated by uterine inversion and hemorrhage (discharged from our L&D yesterday). Bleeding has been steady since she got home and heavier through the night; her husband says she has been soaking pads. Has type 1 vWD and chronic iron deficiency. Bruises easily and has had frequent nosebleeds all her life; says her mother bleeds the same way.
Allergies: latex (rash). No drug allergies.
Meds: ferrous sulfate, vitamin D3, desmopressin nasal PRN.

EXAM on arrival: BP 110/70, HR 98, afebrile. Pale. Uterus firm on palpation. Steady vaginal bleeding.
Labs: Hgb 9.2, plt 250, PT 12, aPTT 38 (mildly prolonged), fibrinogen normal.
Pelvic US: no retained tissue seen.
Given IV desmopressin per hematology by phone; IV fluids; OB called.

At 09:10 she developed severe crampy abdominal pain and felt faint. Pale and diaphoretic. BP 90/60, HR 120. Speculum: cervix dilated with a firm, rounded mass of tissue sitting in the os. Repeat labs Hgb 8, Hct 24%, plt 250, PT 12, PTT 30.

IMPRESSION: secondary postpartum hemorrhage, likely retained tissue despite the ultrasound; vWD.
DISPOSITION: to the OR with OB for evacuation, then admission to obstetrics.

conditions.label: Secondary postpartum hemorrhage due to retained products of conception

reports.text: Specimen: uterine contents, dilation and curettage. Gross: multiple fragments of red-tan soft tissue and blood clot, 4.0 x 3.0 x 1.0 cm in aggregate. Microscopic: chorionic villi and decidua admixed with blood clot.

documents.title: Readmission Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC READMISSION - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 2023-07-04  Discharged: 2023-07-09

Reason: secondary postpartum hemorrhage, postpartum day 3.

She came back through our ED with ongoing bleeding (see ED record). Ultrasound had not shown retained tissue, but on exam there was tissue at a dilated os and she was becoming unstable. Suction dilation and curettage was done the morning of 07/04 with a moderate amount of placental tissue removed; bleeding stopped promptly afterward. Pathology confirmed placental tissue.

On 07/08, one week out from delivery, medicine was asked to see her for fatigue (see consult). Pressures ran soft but she stayed stable. Breastfeeding has been hard - very little milk despite frequent feeds; lactation saw her twice and she is supplementing with formula.

DIAGNOSES: secondary postpartum hemorrhage due to retained products of conception, s/p D&C; recent uterine inversion and primary PPH (07/01); acute blood-loss anemia; type 1 von Willebrand disease; Kallmann syndrome; chronic iron deficiency.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS: unchanged - ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, vitamin D3, desmopressin nasal PRN.

FOLLOW-UP: obstetrics postpartum visit; primary care within 2 weeks.

documents.title: Internal Medicine Inpatient Consultation
documents.author: internal medicine
documents.body:
INTERNAL MEDICINE CONSULTATION
Date: 2023-07-08
Requested by obstetrics for fatigue.

She is a week out from the birth of her son. The delivery was followed by a uterine inversion reduced in the OR (pressure down to 80/40 there, 4 units PRBC) and on day 3 a second bleed needing D&C. Since then she has felt more and more worn out, struggles to manage the baby's care, and her milk supply is poor even though she is putting him to the breast often. Background: type 1 vWD, Kallmann syndrome, iron deficiency.

Exam: pale, pressures mildly low, alert. No fever. Abdomen soft, uterus firm and nontender. No signs of infection.

Impression: postpartum fatigue, most likely from heavy blood loss on top of chronic iron deficiency and the demands of a newborn.
Recommendations: continue oral iron; primary care follow-up within 2 weeks with a CBC; return for worsening dizziness or bleeding.

documents.title: Hospital Records Received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Received from the hospital: two discharge summaries (07/01-07/03 and 07/04-07/09), ED record 07/04, pathology. Indexed and routed to PCP. Pt's husband called asking for a post-hospital appointment; RN to call.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt 3 days after discharge. Bleeding now light, no clots. No fever. Very tired; a bit dizzy getting out of bed, careful on the stairs. Baby doing well; mostly formula now. Taking iron. Reviewed reasons to go back to the ED (soaking a pad an hour, fainting, fever). Video visit booked with PCP for next week, CBC to follow.

documents.title: Telehealth Visit - Post-Hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit; she is at home with the baby asleep beside her. Identity confirmed.

Two hospital stays after her son's birth on 7/1: uterine inversion manually reduced with PPH and 4 units PRBC, then day-3 readmission for secondary PPH with retained placenta, D&C on 7/4. Discharge summaries and pathology reviewed.

Now 18 days postpartum. Bleeding light. Exhausted, short of breath on the stairs, lightheaded when she first stands. Milk never really came in; the baby is on formula and she has stopped trying to pump. Appetite poor. Mood: tearful at times, but says it's mostly fatigue; no thoughts of harming herself or the baby. Husband home on leave for another week.

Meds: ferrous sulfate daily, vitamin D3, desmopressin nasal PRN (has not needed it at home). Hormone replacement still off since the induction cycles.

A/P:
- Acute blood-loss anemia on chronic iron deficiency: CBC tomorrow. Continue iron. Discussed IV iron if no recovery.
- Postpartum, s/p uterine inversion and secondary PPH: OB visit scheduled.
- Hormone replacement: will revisit at the 6-week mark since she is not breastfeeding.
- In-person visit at 6 weeks postpartum. Sooner if dizziness worsens.

documents.title: CBC result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 8.7, up from the hospital nadir. Platelets fine. Message sent: recovering slowly; keep iron daily; see me at 6 weeks.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
OFFICE VISIT - 6 weeks postpartum

First slot of the day so we could draw fasting morning labs.

S: Six weeks after a vaginal delivery complicated by uterine inversion with major hemorrhage (4 u PRBC) and a day-3 secondary PPH with D&C. Still bone-tired; naps whenever the baby does and wakes unrefreshed. Never got a real milk supply and gave up nursing; baby thriving on formula. Gets woozy when she stands up quickly, has had to sit on the floor twice. Not hungry; eats because she should. Lochia finished. No fevers. No headaches or vision change.

Meds: ferrous sulfate 325 daily, vitamin D3, desmopressin nasal PRN (unused). HRT off since last summer's induction cycles.

O: BP 90/60, HR 55. Pale, skin a little dry. Conjunctivae pale. Heart regular, slow, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, uterus not palpable. No edema. PHQ-9 5, no self-harm thoughts.

A/P:
1. Postpartum fatigue with orthostatic dizziness and failed lactation after severe hemorrhage. Anemia is part of it, but the poor milk supply and low pressure after a bleed this size make me want to look at the pituitary too. Drawing BMP, morning cortisol, TSH and free T4, prolactin, CBC and ferritin.
2. Acute blood-loss anemia on iron deficiency - continue iron, recheck counts today.
3. Kallmann syndrome - not breastfeeding and six weeks out, so restarting her estradiol/norethindrone today.
4. Fluids and salt liberally; rise slowly.
Will call with results.

orders.reason: Low morning cortisol and low free T4 after postpartum hemorrhage

documents.title: Results - 8/14 labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Na 130, K 5.2. AM cortisol 3. TSH 0.5 with free T4 0.7 (low). Prolactin 5. Hgb 10.3, ferritin 11.

Sodium low and cortisol and free T4 both low with a TSH that isn't elevated - in the setting of her hemorrhage this needs endocrinology. Referral placed, asked for a soon appointment. Repeat AM cortisol and BMP in 1-2 weeks. Hgb improving.

Spoke with pt by phone, explained results and that endocrinology will evaluate her pituitary function. She has the referral number.

documents.title: Cancelled specialist appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt called: endocrinology appointment for 9/14 - she cancelled it. Baby has had a rough week and she can't make the drive. Says she's feeling a little better. Will call them to rebook. Reminded her the repeat lab order is in for her to get drawn here.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu L deltoid, 2023-24 COVID R deltoid. Non-latex supplies. Firm pressure 2 min each site (vWD), no oozing. Brought the baby along in his car seat. Waited 15 min, fine.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u anemia, 4.5 months postpartum.

Says she is tired but less than in the summer - the baby sleeps longer stretches now. Back at the library part-time since October. Lightheadedness only now and then. Eating better. Back on her estradiol/norethindrone. No nosebleeds lately.

She never rebooked endocrinology; encouraged her again and gave her the number.

Exam: BP and pulse as recorded. Pale-ish but better color. Heart and lungs normal. PHQ-9 3.

A/P:
- Iron deficiency anemia - CBC and ferritin today, continue iron.
- Postpartum hemorrhage, inversion, retained placenta - resolved; cleaning up problem list.
- Kallmann syndrome - continue HRT.
RTC spring for a physical.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Maya - hemoglobin is 11.2 and ferritin 17, both moving in the right direction. Keep up the daily iron. See you in the spring.
